items.t: The cards visible are labelled "Salmon River, Langley" and are mostly rural houses, plus one vacant-land card and the out-of-scope Langley City condo card flagged in the header block. The exact MLS feed filter criteria behind the guide page, and why that condo card is labelled Salmon River in it, are not verified.

Identity: the guide covers the board sub-area "Salmon River" in the Township of Langley — a rural acreage and farm district named for the Salmon River, which runs north to the Fraser River at Fort Langley. "Salmon River" is the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats FVR September 2026 report; the board sub-area code is not verified. Boundaries: the district follows the Salmon River valley between 232 Street and 264 Street, from the Fraser River side south toward 40 Avenue, with Rawlison Crescent and 56 Avenue on the upland side; no Township-published boundary for the sub-area was confirmed, so the exact Township boundary is not verified. Nearby areas: Fort Langley to the north, Otter District to the south, Walnut Grove to the west, Aldergrove to the southeast; the guide page also names Murrayville to the southwest.
Supply shape: effectively all detached — all 5 of the sub-area's September sales were detached. Per-sub-area median prices are NOT published: Not verified.

Where the condo stock concentrates: there is none to concentrate. There are no condo streets in this district: the roads are valley farm roads and upland acreage roads (56 Avenue, Rawlison Crescent, 232 Street, 240 Street, River Road / Glover Road toward Fort Langley), and the Township's development applications route named no condo or townhome project inside the district when the area research checked it.

Poppy Secondary, 23752 52 Ave, Langley; North Otter Elementary, 5370 248 St, Langley. Catchments are address-based: for the sample address 4452 256 Street, the SD35 School Locator returns Elementary — North Otter Elementary; Middle — none shown by the locator; Secondary — D.W. Poppy Secondary; other addresses in the sub-area may fall in different catchments, and no home is promised a specific school. No SD35 school physically inside the Salmon River valley itself was confirmed: Not verified.

Transit and roads: TransLink route 562 (Walnut Grove / Langley Centre) runs on Glover Road via 96 Avenue, 88 Avenue and 202 Street to Carvolth Exchange, serving the Fort Langley edge of the district; no TransLink route was confirmed on 56 Avenue, Rawlison Crescent or the valley roads inside the district. Highway 1 access is south via the 200 Street or 232 Street interchanges; there is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in the district.

The Salmon River valley is Fraser River floodplain land — the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station was originally built to help mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet, provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise, and has flood box gates that close as river levels rise; the Pump Station Upgrades are a live Township project, with Council having authorized staff to proceed with detailed design and tendering. Parcel-level floodplain mapping and watercourse setback distances: Not verified. No recreation centre or library branch inside the district was confirmed: Not verified. Health care: Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway, Langley (24/7 emergency), southwest of the district, and the Langley Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 202 - 20434 64th Avenue, Langley; a hospital or clinic inside the district is not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Salmon River Guide

items.t: Township zoning and SSMUH — Bylaw 6020: rural land is under Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (the district's farm and acreage homes sit in the rural zones, including RU-2; the RU-2 minimum lot area and frontage were not confirmed from a readable bylaw section: Not verified; zone assignments for a parcel come from the bylaw Map Schedules through the Township's GeoSource). The Township's SSMUH rules under Bylaw 6020, adopted November 18, 2024, allow 3 units on eligible lots of 280 m² or smaller and 4 units on larger eligible lots up to 4,050 m², with lots over 4,050 m² ineligible for the multi-unit tiers and NO 6-plex tier in the Township; on lots larger than 4,050 m² the rules allow one secondary suite or one accessory dwelling unit in addition to the primary unit, depending on zoning. The Township caps a secondary suite at 120 m² maximum gross floor area (Bylaw No. 2500, s. 102). In Bylaw 2500, s. 102, a "coach house" is an accessory dwelling unit located only within the second storey of a detached garage — a fee-simple second unit under the zoning bylaw, never strata. On Salmon River acreages, that suite/accessory route — not a strata condo building — is the added-unit route the rules describe.

items.t: (2) A feed card outside the guide's stated rural scope — a Langley City condo unit at Cornerstone North by Marcon is labelled "Salmon River" and surfaces inside a guide whose own copy is about acreages, farms and wells.

The pump station is a live capital project. Council has authorized staff to proceed with detailed design and tendering for the Salmon River Pump Station Upgrades — flood infrastructure, not strata infrastructure, is the district's active construction story, and flood status drives insurance and lending on valley parcels.

Wells and septic are the district's "strata documents." Rural properties may use wells searchable in the provincial GWELLS database (well reports due within 90 days of work on a well), and Fraser Health's authorized-person filings are the paper trail for an onsite sewerage system. Those filings are the paper trail a buyer here actually reviews.
The neighbouring district is not a proxy, in either direction.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Salmon River
Streets, schools and getting around Salmon River

items.t: Salmon River is a Township of Langley rural district along the Salmon River in the township's northwest, north of the Otter area and south of Fort Langley; "Salmon River" is also the Fraser Valley board sub-area name used in the SnapStats FVR report. No Township-published boundary for the sub-area was confirmed.

Schools: SD35 catchments are address-based. For the sample address 4452 256 Street, the SD35 School Locator returns North Otter Elementary and D.W. Poppy Secondary, with no middle school shown; Coghlan Fundamental Elementary, 4452 256 Street, is a district school of choice on the upland east side, its position inside this board sub-area not confirmed. No SD35 school physically inside the Salmon River valley itself was confirmed.

Flood: the valley is Fraser River floodplain land — the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station was built to mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet, provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise, has flood box gates that close as river levels rise, and is in detailed design and tendering for upgrades Council authorized.

Parent community (Langley combined) attached median is $611,000 — a Langley-wide combined condo+towhome figure, never a Salmon River townhome figure; the report publishes no Salmon River–specific median.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Salmon River

items.t: The governing fact for this sub-area: there is no townhouse strata stock to apply strata diligence to: Most Salmon River properties are non-strata freehold acreages; where a strata parcel exists, BC strata law is the Strata Property Act and strata disputes go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal. A buyer told a valley property is a "townhouse" should verify title form first — on the verified record here, it will be a freehold acreage house.

ALR stratification bar: an ALR residence cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09, s.6; Strata Property Act s.239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s.21(1)). Farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve in places — confirm a specific parcel on the ALC maps — and that bar is the structural reason townhouse strata do not appear on ALR valley land.

ALC residence caps: principal residence at most 500 m²; suite within the principal residence only; one additional residence at most 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less and at most 186 m² over 40 ha, subject to Township bylaws. Farm-class thresholds in full three-tier form: $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of land value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by October 31 — a flat "$2,500+" statement is an error.

Township of Langley zoning and SSMUH: rural land is under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (farm and acreage homes sit in the rural zones, including RU-2; the RU-2 minimum lot area and frontage were not confirmed from a readable bylaw section — not confirmed). The Township Official Community Plan and the Rural Plan govern the district.

Strata standard block (applies only if a genuine strata parcel is ever verified here): Form B diligence (Strata Property Act s.59 — fees, amounts owing, approved levies, CRF balance, insurance summary, with rules, budget, Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page); depreciation reports every five years for 5+ lot stratas since July 1, 2024; CRF minimum 10% of the operating budget since Nov 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since Nov 24, 2022 (flag any directory "rentals not allowed" line void in-entry); only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2, Regulation 7.01 exemptions expanded May 1, 2023).

Watercourse setbacks: the Salmon River is a salmon-bearing watercourse, so setbacks and riparian rules can limit building envelopes near the river — parcel-level setback distances for a specific parcel: Not confirmed; check with the Township before planning a build.

: FTHB GST rebate — Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026 per CRA News No. 122 (100% of GST to $1M, phasing to $1.5M, maximum $50,000, agreements Mar 20, 2025–2031); New Housing Rebate 36% / maximum $6,300 / $350K–$450K; PTT with the first-time buyer exemption (first $500,000 exempt at FMV $835,000 or less, partial to $860,000) and the newly built home exemption (full to $1,100,000, eliminated at $1,150,000) — confirm the farm/ALR position for a specific parcel; Home Buyers' Plan $60,000; FHSA $40,000 lifetime / $8,000 per year; CMHC premiums 0.6%–4.5%. REDMA s.21 7-day rescission and s.18 trust deposits apply where a presale exists — no presale is verified in this sub-area.

items.t: The upland edge of the district runs on 56 Avenue and Rawlison Crescent, and that upland/valley split is the geography that decides whether any attached product could exist here at all.

blocks.text: Salmon River Condos and Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: (SnapStats, September 2026)

No named townhome complex is verified inside the district either: the same Township route named no townhome project, and the district's homes are farm and acreage houses on large rural lots along the valley and the 56 Avenue upland.
Most Salmon River properties are non-strata freehold acreages, so a unit marketed here as a condo or townhome should be checked against its title and strata plan before it is treated as strata stock.

blocks.text: Salmon River Condos and Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Rural land here is under Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500, and zone assignments for a specific parcel come from the bylaw map schedules through the Township's GeoSource mapping, not from a listing's zone label.

The Township's small-scale multi-unit housing position does not create townhome product in the valley: properties that do not meet the eligibility criteria — including lots larger than 4,050 square metres — are eligible for one residential unit plus one secondary suite or accessory dwelling unit (ADU), and Salmon River acreages are generally above that lot-size line.

If a strata parcel does surface here, provincial strata law is the frame: rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022, and the Form B Information Certificate is the diligence document for fees, levies and the depreciation report.

blocks.text: Salmon River Condos and Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Salmon River is a salmon-bearing watercourse, and Metro Vancouver watershed material covers the Salmon River watershed — riparian setbacks can limit the building envelope on parcels near the river, separate from the flood question.

Rural properties here may use wells: the provincial GWELLS database holds registered well records and mapped aquifers, and well reports are due within 90 days of constructing, altering or decommissioning a well — pull the parcel's record before closing.
There is no recreation centre or library branch inside the district on the Township facility list; the nearest Township facilities are in Fort Langley and Walnut Grove.

blocks.text: Salmon River Condos and Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: The Township's 2026 budget raised property taxes 3.97 percent in total — 0.90 percent for core municipal services, 1.59 percent for RCMP, 1.26 percent for fire and 0.22 percent for bylaws — per the Township's 2026 property tax newsletter.

A Salmon River acreage on well and septic does not pay the Township flat-rate water and sewer charges a serviced strata unit pays — servicing, not the tax rate, is the cost split between the valley acreages and Township townhome product elsewhere.

blocks.text: Salmon River Condos and Townhomes: getting around

items.t: TransLink route 562 (Walnut Grove / Langley Centre) runs on Glover Road via 96 Avenue, 88 Avenue and 202 Street to Carvolth Exchange, serving the Fort Langley edge of the district; no TransLink route was confirmed on 56 Avenue, Rawlison Crescent or the valley roads inside the district.
There is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in the district; Highway 1 access is south via the 200 Street or 232 Street interchanges.
The district's own roads are 56 Avenue and Rawlison Crescent on the upland, 232 Street and 240 Street as the north-south edges, and River Road and Glover Road toward Fort Langley.

blocks.text: Salmon River Condos and Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Confirm Agricultural Land Reserve status on the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR maps for the exact parcel, because valley farm land is in the reserve only in places and ALR status governs second dwellings and subdivision.
Pull the GWELLS well record and the Fraser Health sewerage filings for the parcel: a well or septic system with no filings is a servicing risk that no listing document will surface.

Check riparian setbacks with the Township before planning any build near the river: the Salmon River is salmon-bearing, and the watershed material does not state a setback distance for a specific parcel.
